source_batch.unit_label: Module D unit 1 (courseware unit 26): the compliance function in banks

facts.statement: Compliance is the act of observing laws, rules, regulations and various codes of conduct, including the voluntary ones; while most arise from external requirements, adherence to the organisation's own internal rules, policies and procedures, and acting in accordance with ethical practices, is equally important. Compliance risk, as the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision paper of April 2005 defines it (as the courseware quotes it), is the risk of legal or regulatory sanction, material financial loss, or loss to reputation a bank may suffer as a result of its failure to comply with laws, regulations, rules, related self-regulatory organisation standards and codes of conduct applicable to its banking services. Compliance risk arises from non-adherence to a set of laws, rules, regulations, practices, self-regulatory organisation standards and codes of conduct, grouped into internal compliance (applicable to all employees) and regulatory and legal compliance (applicable to the bank as a whole). The significance of the compliance function is that it promotes uniform and proper behaviour by the stakeholders, especially employees, reduces systemic vulnerability, minimises deviations and aberrations, allows identification of violations for prompt corrective action and improves corporate governance in the bank.

The courseware ties compliance risk to other risks: regulatory risk (the consequences of non-compliance, including financial harm, litigation and enforcement); operational risk (loss from inadequate or failed processes, people and systems, so compliance risk is "operational risk come alive"); legal risk (lawsuits, adverse judgements or unenforceable contracts); reputational risk (negative publicity leading to loss of confidence, business and market value, and liquidity risk); annihilation risk (regulatory action of closing down the business); business risk; and strategic risk. On cyber security, compliance with cyber resilience guidelines aims to address confidentiality breaches, availability breaches (systems intact but services unavailable) and integrity breaches (corruption of data or of information processing methods). Penalties for non-compliance, and "name and shame", add to the cost of non-compliance, so compliance should be an everyday practice supported by empowered employees.

A bank has a Board-approved compliance policy that spells out its compliance philosophy; its expectations on compliance culture covering tone from the top, accountability, incentive structure and effective communication and challenge; the structure and role of the compliance function; the role of the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO); and the processes for identifying, assessing, monitoring, managing and reporting on compliance risk throughout the bank. The policy adequately reflects the size, complexity and compliance risk profile of the bank, expectations on compliance to all applicable statutory provisions, rules and regulations, codes of conduct including voluntary ones and the bank's own internal rules, and creates a disincentive structure for compliance breaches. The bank develops and maintains a quality assurance and improvement programme covering all aspects of the compliance function, subject to independent external review periodically (at least once in three years). The policy lays special thrust on building compliance culture and on vetting the quality of supervisory and regulatory compliance reports to RBI by the top executives and the non-executive Chairman or Chairman and the Audit Committee of the Board (ACB). The policy is reviewed at least once a year.

Compliance principles, process and procedures (courseware, from the 2007 guidelines): the compliance department at the Head office plays the central role in identifying the level of compliance risk in each business line, product and process and issues instructions or formulates proposals for mitigation of risk, and periodically circulates instances of compliance failures with instructions for prevention; inspection and audit findings are a feedback mechanism; it incorporates a robust mechanism to ensure that regulatory guidelines are promptly issued to the organisation and to monitor compliance; it serves as the reference point for operational departments seeking clarification of regulations; it proactively identifies, documents and assesses compliance risks of business activities and products (the CCO is a member of the new product committee, and new products are intensively monitored for the first six months); functionwise compliance manuals are developed with the compliance department; it interacts with the legal, operational risk management, taxation and audit or inspection departments; compliance officers have access to all information they need and the right to conduct investigations and report findings to the CCO; the function monitors and tests compliance through sufficient and representative testing and reports the results to senior management; compliance staff may use external experts for an investigation at the CCO's discretion; the function is free to report irregularities to senior management without fear of disfavour and has the right of direct access to the Board or the Audit Committee, and the CCO meets the Audit Committee at least annually; an annual report on the compliance function, including failures and breaches, is placed before the Board or ACB and non-compliance with regulatory guidelines and actions taken against the bank is disclosed in the annual report; staff accountability is examined for compliance failures and compliance record is weighed in staff performance appraisal.

facts.statement: The compliance function runs under a compliance programme that sets out its planned activities, is risk-based and is subject to oversight by the head of compliance. The compliance function may have specific statutory responsibilities such as the anti-money laundering officer role. Banks carry out an annual compliance risk assessment and prepare a plan to manage the risks; the annual review broadly covers compliance failures and the steps to avoid recurrence, the major regulatory guidelines issued during the year and the steps taken to ensure compliance, independence of the compliance function, its scope, compliance procedures, the system of internal control to minimise compliance risk, compliance with fair practices codes and standards set by self-regulatory bodies and accounting standards, progress in rectification of significant deficiencies pointed out in internal audit, statutory and RBI inspection reports, and the strategy for the next year. Compliance units devise a time bound strategy to meet the points of the Monitorable Action Plan or Risk Mitigation Plan prescribed in the supervisory process. Apart from the annual review, the CCO puts up a monthly report on compliance risk to the senior management or CEO and a brief report quarterly to the Board, ACB or Board Committee as the case may be; instances of material compliance failures that may attract significant legal or regulatory sanctions, financial loss or loss of reputation are reported promptly. The compliance function is subject to annual review by internal audit, whose risk assessment methodology includes compliance risk. The function advises and assists senior management through written guidance and manuals. For cross-border business, the organisation and structure of the compliance function are consistent with local legal and regulatory requirements and local compliance responsibilities are carried out by individuals with local knowledge, with oversight by the head of compliance.

facts.statement: The scope of the compliance function covers: statutory compliance (the Banking Regulation Act, the Reserve Bank of India Act, the Foreign Exchange Management Act, the Prevention of Money Laundering Act); regulatory compliance (guidelines of regulators such as RBI, SEBI and IRDA); codes of conduct (guidelines of organisations such as IBA, BCSBI, FEDAI and FIMDA); accounting standards (as framed by ICAI); the listing agreement (if the bank is listed on a stock exchange, it complies with the listing agreement); and internal compliances (process and policy compliances codified in the bank's instruction manual, circulars and policies). Subsidiaries and Regional Rural Banks, which are closely connected to the bank's name and fame, also establish a compliance function with the approval of their Boards, with compliance departments responsible for the function in their institutions and submitting periodic reports to their Boards; they arrange quarterly compliance status certificates to the bank's CCO in a consolidated format to the bank's ACB; and the Chairman or directors representing the bank on their Boards ensure that the applicable guidelines are implemented and advise the bank's CCO of any failures and corrective steps.

Appointment and status of the CCO: the CCO is appointed for a minimum fixed tenure of not less than 3 years; transfer or removal before the tenure ends is possible only in exceptional circumstances with the explicit prior approval of the Board after a well-defined and transparent internal administrative procedure. Eligibility: a senior executive of the bank, preferably in the rank of a General Manager or equivalent (not below two levels from the CEO), who could also be recruited from the market; age not more than 55 years; overall experience of at least 15 years in banking or financial services, of which at least 5 years in audit, finance, compliance, legal or risk management; good understanding of the industry and risk management, knowledge of regulations and legal framework and sensitivity to supervisors' expectations; ability to exercise judgement independently with the freedom and authority to interact with regulators directly; and no vigilance case or adverse observation from RBI pending against the candidate. The selection is based on a well-defined process and the recommendations of a senior executive level selection committee constituted by the Board, which recommends names in order of merit with the Board taking the final decision. A prior intimation goes to the Department of Supervision, RBI Central Office, before the appointment or premature transfer or removal, with a detailed profile and a fit and proper certification by the MD and CEO and the rationale for changes. Banks already having a CCO could follow the process within six months and could reappoint the incumbent if he or she met the requirements.

Reporting line and authority: the CCO has direct reporting lines to the MD and CEO and/or the Board or its Audit Committee (ACB); if the CCO reports to the MD and CEO, the ACB meets the CCO quarterly one-to-one without senior management including the MD and CEO. The CCO has no reporting relationship with the business verticals and is given no business targets; the performance appraisal of the CCO is reviewed by the Board or ACB. The CCO and the compliance function have the authority to communicate with any staff member and have access to all records or files necessary for their responsibilities, flowing from the compliance policy. The duties of the compliance function include at least: to apprise the Board and senior management of regulations, rules, standards and developments; to clarify compliance issues; to assess compliance risk at least once a year and develop a risk-oriented activity plan for compliance assessment, submitted to the ACB for approval and made available to internal audit; to report promptly any major changes or observations on compliance risk to the Board, ACB or MD and CEO; to report periodically on compliance failures or breaches to the Board or ACB and circulate them to the concerned functional heads; to monitor and periodically test compliance through sufficient and representative testing, placing the results before the Board, ACB or MD and CEO; to examine sustenance of compliance as part of testing and annual assessment; and to ensure compliance of supervisory observations of RBI and other directions in letter and spirit in a time bound and sustainable manner. The compliance function is itself subject to internal audit.

There is no dual hatting: the CCO is not given any responsibility that brings an element of conflict of interest, especially a role relating to business; roles that do not attract direct conflict, such as the anti-money laundering officer, may be performed by the CCO in banks where the principle of proportionality (size, complexity, risk management strategy and structures) justifies it. The CCO is not a member of any committee that brings the role in conflict with responsibility as a member, including any committee dealing with purchases or sanctions; if a member, the CCO has only an advisory role. The typical core elements of the CCO's mandate include design and maintenance of the compliance framework, training on regulatory and conduct risks, and effective communication of compliance expectations. The Board of Directors is overall responsible for overseeing effective management of the compliance function and compliance risk, and the MD and CEO ensures the presence of an independent compliance function and adherence to the compliance policy.

The CCO's responsibilities in risk based supervision (as the courseware reports them): co-ordinating with Head Office departments for information and data during the Inspection for Supervisory Evaluation (ISE) by the RBI supervisory team under the Supervisory Programme for Assessment of Risk and Capital (SPARC); arranging the exit meeting with the bank's top executives; co-ordinating the supervisory meeting of the top executive with RBI top management; presenting the Risk Assessment Report with annexes, the Risk Mitigation Plans and the bank's supervisory rating to the Board or committees immediately on receipt; submitting the action plan and compliance on RAR and RMP to the Board or committees for approval and to RBI until compliance is accepted, with the compliance department furnishing RAR or RMP points where compliance is accepted and the action taken to the Inspection and Audit Department for feedback on sustainability; and reporting compliance status and emerging issues at domestic branches to the top management and ACB or Board. The CCO also ensures formulation and updating of compliance rules with the functional departments, especially on KYC, anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism, deposits and services, advances and FEMA guidelines.

items.title: What compliance and compliance risk mean
items.core_explanation_md:
**Compliance** is **observing laws, rules, regulations and codes of conduct**, including the **voluntary** ones. External requirements dominate, but the bank's **own policies and procedures** and **ethical practice** matter equally.

**Compliance risk** (BCBS, April 2005, as the courseware quotes it): the risk of **legal or regulatory sanction, material financial loss or loss to reputation** from **failing to comply** with laws, rules, regulations, **self-regulatory organisation standards** and **codes of conduct**.

| Kind | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| **Internal compliance** | **All employees** |
| **Regulatory and legal compliance** | **The bank as a whole** |

**Why the function matters:** it promotes **uniform, proper behaviour**, **reduces systemic vulnerability**, **minimises deviations**, helps **spot violations** for prompt correction and **improves governance**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Compliance goes beyond what is legally binding to integrity, ethical conduct and good governance.

items.title: Compliance principles, process and procedures (courseware)
items.core_explanation_md:
Held at needs_review: the courseware reports the **2007 guidelines**.

- The **Head office compliance department** plays the **central role** in identifying **compliance risk** by business line, product and process, and issues **instructions** and **circulates failures**.

- It **proactively assesses compliance risk of products**: the **CCO sits on the new product committee**; new products are **monitored intensively for six months**.
- **Function-wise compliance manuals** are built with operating departments.
- It talks regularly to **legal, operational risk, taxation and audit** departments.
- **Compliance officers** can see **all information** and **investigate**; external experts may be used at the **CCO's discretion**.
- **Testing:** **sufficient and representative** compliance testing, results to **senior management**.
- **Independence:** free to report irregularities **without fear**, with **direct access to the Board or Audit Committee**; the **CCO meets the Audit Committee at least annually**.
- An **annual compliance report** goes to the **Board or ACB**; **non-compliance and penalties** are disclosed in the **annual report**.
- **Staff accountability** for compliance failures; compliance record counts in **appraisal**.

items.title: The CCO's reporting line, authority and duties
items.core_explanation_md:
**Reporting line:** direct to the **MD and CEO** and/or the **Board or its Audit Committee (ACB)**. If to the MD and CEO, the **ACB meets the CCO quarterly, one-to-one**, **without senior management** present. **No reporting to business verticals; no business targets.** The Board or ACB reviews the CCO's **performance appraisal**.

**Authority:** to talk to **any staff member** and see **all records and files** needed, flowing from the **compliance policy**.

**Duties (at least)**

1. **Apprise** the Board and senior management of **regulations, standards and developments**.
2. **Clarify** compliance issues.
3. **Assess compliance risk at least once a year** and prepare a **risk-oriented activity plan**, approved by the **ACB** and shared with **internal audit**.
4. **Report promptly** major changes or observations on compliance risk.
5. **Report compliance failures or breaches** periodically to the Board or ACB and to functional heads.
6. **Test compliance** by sufficient and representative testing and report the results.
7. **Examine sustenance** of compliance.
8. **Ensure compliance with RBI supervisory observations** in letter and spirit, time-bound and sustainable.

The compliance function itself is **subject to internal audit**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The one-to-one meeting protects the CCO's independence from the executive management.

items.title: Dual hatting, committees and who is accountable
items.core_explanation_md:
**No dual hatting.** The CCO must not hold a role that brings a **conflict of interest**, **especially a business role**.

- **Permitted where proportionality justifies it** (size, complexity, risk management strategy and structures): roles **without direct conflict**, such as **anti-money laundering officer**.
- The CCO is **not a member of any committee** that conflicts with the role, **including purchases or sanctions committees**; if a member, only **advisory**.

**Mandate (core elements):** **design and maintenance of the compliance framework**, **training on regulatory and conduct risks**, **communication of compliance expectations**.

**Responsibility**

| | Responsible for |
| --- | --- |
| **Board of Directors** | **Overall oversight** of the compliance function and compliance risk |
| **MD and CEO** | Ensuring an **independent compliance function** and **adherence to the compliance policy** |
